stem: On which date day and night are of equal duration?
expl: Day and night are of equal duration on the day of the equinox. Equinox literally means "equal day and equal night". An equinox is an astronomical event in which Sun is vertically overhead of the equator, which occurs twice each year, i.e., 20/21st March and 22/23rd September. Therefore, in the given options 23rd September is the correct answer.

stem: Where are day and night equal throughout the year?
expl: Day and night are of equal duration on The Equator (12 hours each). The duration of day and night varies in the direction of north or south to the equator. There is no winter season on the equator. It only experiences wet and dry weather.

stem: At the time the summer solstice in the northern hemisphere the length of the day will be 12 hours at the :
expl: Two types of solstices occur in a year (i) Summer Solstice and (ii) Winter Solstice. The sun reaches the Tropic of Cancer in the month of June in the Northern Hemisphere and the Summer Solstice takes place, just opposite to it in the Southern Hemisphere the Winter Solstice takes place. At the time of Summer Solstice the longest day and shortest night occur in Northern Hemisphere, but in the Southern Hemisphere the shortest day and longest night occur. At the same time, there is not much difference in days and nights at the Equator. Therefore option (d) is the correct answer.

stem:
On June 21 every year, which of the following latitude(s) experience(s) a sunlight of more than 12 hours?
1. Equator 2. Tropic of Cancer
3. Tropic of Capricorn 4. Arctic Circle
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
expl: On June 21 every year, among the given latitudes, the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle (as these are in Northern Hemisphere) experience a sunlight of more than 12 hours. On 21st June, the Northern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun. The rays of the Sun fall directly on the Tropic of Cancer. As a result, these areas receive more heat. The areas near the poles receive less heat as the rays of the Sun are slanting. The North Pole is inclined towards the Sun and the places beyond the Arctic Circle experience continuous daylight for about six months. Since a large portion of the Northern Hemisphere is getting more light from the Sun, it is summer in the regions north of the equator. The longest day and the shortest night at these places occur on around 21st June. This position of the Earth in Northern Hemisphere is called the Summer Solstice. At this time in the Southern Hemisphere all these conditions are reversed. It is winter season there. The nights are longer than the days.

stem:
Consider the following statements :
Statement I :Scientific studies suggest that a shift is taking place in the Earth's rotation and axis.
Statement II :Solar flares and associated coronal mass ejections bombarded the Earth's outermost atmosphere with tremendous amount of energy.
Statement III :As the Earth's polar ice melts, the water tends to move towards the equator.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

options.label: a
options.text: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I.

options.label: b
options.text: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I.

options.label: c
options.text: Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I.

options.label: d
options.text: Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct.

expl: Over the past several hundred years, the position of the Earth’s rotation axis has shifted slightly, and the length of the day has increased by a very small but measurable amount. Therefore, Statement I is correct. Solar flares and the often-associated coronal mass ejections (CMEs) indeed deliver a large amount of energy to the Earth’s outermost atmosphere (mainly the upper ionosphere/thermosphere and the magnetosphere). However, this energy largely remains confined to the upper atmosphere and the magnetosphere; its effect on the Earth’s mass distribution or on the solid body of the Earth is generally not a primary driver compared with large-scale mass redistribution Process. Due to the melting of Greenland, Antarctica, and other ice sheets, the solid ice mass reaches the oceans in the form of water. Thus, both Statement II and Statement III are factually correct. ∴ Only Statement III provides the scientific explanation for the changes occurring in the Earth’s rotation and axis (Statement I). Statement II merely describes the impact of solar flares on the upper atmosphere, not the shift of the Earth’s axis.
